synthesis_note: This narrative review proposes a geroscience-informed biopsychosocial framework for managing myofascial pain in older adults, integrating biological aging mechanisms, psychological therapies, and social considerations. While substantive content is developed for biological and psychological domains, social factors are mentioned but less elaborated. The integration is descriptive rather than mechanistic, representing a multifactorial rather than truly integrative BPS approach. The paper addresses conceptual gaps in geriatric pain management but lacks high-quality geriatric-specific evidence for many proposed interventions.

synthesis_note: This narrative review proposes a mechanistic triadic model linking insecure attachment, C-tactile fiber dysfunction, and oxytocinergic system alterations as core pathophysiological mechanisms in fibromyalgia and central sensitivity syndromes. It integrates biological (HPA axis, ANS, neuroplasticity), psychological (attachment, threat-soothing imbalance), and social (caregiver-infant bonding, bio-behavioral synchrony) domains through developmental pathways. The paper demonstrates substantive three-domain integration with explicit causal mechanisms, distinguishing it from pseudo-BPS reviews. However, it lacks formal definitions for most psychological constructs and relies heavily on theoretical models rather than empirical validation.

It substantively covers psychological constructs (fear-avoidance, expectations, self-efficacy) and mentions biological (structural, chronic conditions) and social (support, insurance) factors. Social mechanisms include socioeconomic stress, social support buffering, and interpersonal dynamics affecting pain perception. synthesis_note: This narrative review advocates for the biopsychosocial model in chronic pain management, describing how biological, psychological, and social factors interact in a descriptive rather than mechanistic way. It provides a comprehensive overview of risk factors, patient attitudes, and treatment approaches, positioning BPS as a holistic framework. The paper does not critically examine the integration depth of BPS in the literature it reviews, nor does it assess whether the three domains are genuinely interrelated or merely listed together.
coding_rationale: The paper presents all three BPS domains substantively with named constructs and describes their integration descriptively rather than mechanistically. The typology is 'multifactorial' because all domains are present and related, but the integration lacks specified pathways. The triadic integration is 'descriptive' as the paper describes a holistic approach without detailing mechanistic connections between domains.
